subject: maths
title: Adding and Subtracting 2-Digit Numbers
seo_title: Year 2 Adding and Subtracting 2-Digit Numbers Worksheets: Split Strategy, Jump Strategy and Bar Models
standard_text: Add and subtract one- and two-digit numbers, representing problems using number sentences, and solve using part-part-whole reasoning and a variety of calculation strategies
meta_desc: Free Year 2 maths worksheets on adding and subtracting 2-digit numbers, matched to the Australian Curriculum (AC9M2N04): add and subtract tens, the split strategy with MAB, the jump strategy, regrouping and part-part-whole bar models. 100 questions with an answer key.
key_big: Add tens to tens and ones to ones. Regroup when you need to.
key_sub: 36 + 27: 30 + 20 = 50 and 6 + 7 = 13, so 63. For 52 − 17 there are not enough ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 12 − 7 = 5 and 4 − 1 = 3, so 35.
body_html:
The idea: tens with tens, ones with ones

A 2-digit number is made of tens and ones. 45 is 4 tens and 5 ones. Add tens to tens. Add ones to ones.

Number sentenceAnswerWhat changes
45 + 3075the tens: 4 + 3 = 7
45 + 348the ones: 5 + 3 = 8
76 − 4036the tens: 7 − 4 = 3

The split strategy

Split both numbers into tens and ones. Add the tens. Add the ones. Then put them together.

If there are 10 or more ones, regroup: 10 ones make 1 ten.

The jump strategy

Start at the first number on an empty number line. Jump the tens, then the ones. Jumping to the next ten makes it easier.

Jump back

What is 63 − 28?

63 − 20 = 43. 43 − 3 = 40. 40 − 5 = 35.

Answer: 35

Subtracting with regrouping

Sometimes there are not enough ones to take away. Regroup 1 ten as 10 ones.

Part-part-whole bar models

Two parts make the whole. To find the whole, add. To find a missing part, subtract.

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Taking the smaller digit from the larger one: 52 − 17 = 452 − 7 cannot be done. Regroup 1 ten: 12 − 7 = 5. Answer: 35
Adding tens as ones: 45 + 30 = 4830 is 3 tens. Add it to the tens: 75
Forgetting to regroup: 36 + 27 = 536 + 7 = 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones. Answer: 63
Writing 50 and 13 side by side: 36 + 27 = 513Add the parts: 50 + 13 = 63

faq.q: What does Year 2 learn about adding and subtracting in the Australian Curriculum?
faq.a: Year 2 students add and subtract one- and two-digit numbers. They write number sentences, use part-part-whole thinking and choose strategies such as the split strategy and the jump strategy.
The split strategy splits numbers into tens and ones. For 36 + 27, add 30 + 20 = 50 and 6 + 7 = 13, then 50 + 13 = 63.
The jump strategy uses an empty number line. Start at one number and jump the tens, then the ones: for 38 + 25, jump +20 to 58, +2 to 60 and +3 to 63.

faq.q: What is regrouping in Year 2 subtraction?
faq.a: Regrouping (also called trading) means swapping 1 ten for 10 ones when there are not enough ones. For 52 − 17, 52 becomes 4 tens and 12 ones, so the answer is 35.

items.e: 30 is 3 tens. Add the tens: 4 tens + 3 tens = 7 tens. The ones stay the same. 45 + 30 = 75.

items.q: The MAB show 76. 4 tens are crossed out. What is 76 − 40?
items.e: 40 is 4 tens. Take away the tens: 7 tens − 4 tens = 3 tens. The ones stay the same. 76 − 40 = 36.

items.q: Count on in tens. What is 23 + 30?
items.e: Count on 3 tens from 23: 33, 43, 53. The ones stay the same. 23 + 30 = 53.

items.q: Count back in tens. What is 82 − 40?
items.e: Count back 4 tens from 82: 72, 62, 52, 42. The ones stay the same. 82 − 40 = 42.

items.q: What is 10 more than 57?
items.e: 10 more means 1 more ten. 5 tens become 6 tens. The ones stay the same: 67.

items.q: What is 10 less than 63?
items.e: 10 less means 1 less ten. 6 tens become 5 tens. The ones stay the same: 53.

items.q: You add 30 to 24. Which digit changes?
items.e: 30 is 3 tens, so only the tens digit changes: 24 + 30 = 54.
20 is 2 tens. Add the tens: 3 tens + 2 tens = 5 tens. The ones stay the same. 31 + 20 = 51.

items.q: What is 15 + 40?
items.e: 40 is 4 tens. Add the tens: 1 ten + 4 tens = 5 tens. The ones stay the same. 15 + 40 = 55.

items.q: What is 18 + 30?

items.q: What is 25 + 50?

items.q: What is 72 − 60?
items.e: 60 is 6 tens. Take away the tens: 7 tens − 6 tens = 1 ten. The ones stay the same. 72 − 60 = 12.

items.q: The MAB show 51. 2 tens are crossed out. What is 51 − 20?
items.e: 20 is 2 tens. Take away the tens: 5 tens − 2 tens = 3 tens. The ones stay the same. 51 − 20 = 31.

items.q: What is 81 − 50?
items.e: 50 is 5 tens. Take away the tens: 8 tens − 5 tens = 3 tens. The ones stay the same. 81 − 50 = 31.

items.q: What is 54 − 30?
items.e: 30 is 3 tens. Take away the tens: 5 tens − 3 tens = 2 tens. The ones stay the same. 54 − 30 = 24.

items.q: Count on in tens. What is 74 + 40?
items.e: Count on 4 tens from 74: 84, 94, 104, 114. After 94 comes 104. The ones stay the same. 74 + 40 = 114.

items.q: What is 86 + 50?
items.e: Tens: 8 tens + 5 tens = 13 tens = 130. The ones stay the same. 86 + 50 = 136.

items.q: Find the missing number: 36 + ? = 76
items.e: The ones stay at 6. The tens go from 3 to 7. That is 4 tens: 40. Check: 36 + 40 = 76.

items.q: Find the missing number: 93 − ? = 53
items.e: The ones stay at 3. The tens go from 9 down to 5. That is 4 tens: 40. Check: 93 − 40 = 53.

items.q: Which shows 36 split into tens and ones?
items.e: 36 is 3 tens and 6 ones: 30 + 6. The 3 is in the tens place, so it is worth 30.

items.q: Which is the same as 36 + 27?
items.e: Split both numbers into tens and ones: 36 = 30 + 6 and 27 = 20 + 7. So 36 + 27 = 30 + 20 + 6 + 7.

items.q: The MAB show two numbers. What is 28 + 15?
items.e: Count the longs: 2 + 1 = 3 tens. Count the minis: 8 + 5 = 13 ones. Regroup 10 ones as 1 ten: 4 tens and 3 ones. 28 + 15 = 43.

items.q: The MAB show two numbers. What is 47 + 26?
items.e: Count the longs: 4 + 2 = 6 tens. Count the minis: 7 + 6 = 13 ones. Regroup 10 ones as 1 ten: 7 tens and 3 ones. 47 + 26 = 73.

items.q: The MAB show two numbers. What is 39 + 44?
items.e: Count the longs: 3 + 4 = 7 tens. Count the minis: 9 + 4 = 13 ones. Regroup 10 ones as 1 ten: 8 tens and 3 ones. 39 + 44 = 83.

items.q: The MAB show two numbers. What is 58 + 25?
items.e: Count the longs: 5 + 2 = 7 tens. Count the minis: 8 + 5 = 13 ones. Regroup 10 ones as 1 ten: 8 tens and 3 ones. 58 + 25 = 83.

items.q: Use the split strategy. What is 46 + 38?
items.e: Split both numbers: 46 = 40 + 6 and 38 = 30 + 8. Tens: 40 + 30 = 70. Ones: 6 + 8 = 14. 14 ones is 1 ten and 4 ones. 70 + 14 = 84.

items.q: Use the split strategy. What is 57 + 29?
items.e: Split both numbers: 57 = 50 + 7 and 29 = 20 + 9. Tens: 50 + 20 = 70. Ones: 7 + 9 = 16. 16 ones is 1 ten and 6 ones. 70 + 16 = 86.

items.q: Use the split strategy. What is 64 + 28?
items.e: Split both numbers: 64 = 60 + 4 and 28 = 20 + 8. Tens: 60 + 20 = 80. Ones: 4 + 8 = 12. 12 ones is 1 ten and 2 ones. 80 + 12 = 92.

items.q: Use the split strategy. What is 35 + 47?
items.e: Split both numbers: 35 = 30 + 5 and 47 = 40 + 7. Tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Ones: 5 + 7 = 12. 12 ones is 1 ten and 2 ones. 70 + 12 = 82.

items.q: Use the split strategy. What is 68 + 45?
items.e: Split both numbers: 68 = 60 + 8 and 45 = 40 + 5. Tens: 60 + 40 = 100. Ones: 8 + 5 = 13. 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones. 100 + 13 = 113.

items.q: Use the split strategy. What is 76 + 58?
items.e: Split both numbers: 76 = 70 + 6 and 58 = 50 + 8. Tens: 70 + 50 = 120. Ones: 6 + 8 = 14. 14 ones is 1 ten and 4 ones. 120 + 14 = 134.

items.e: From 45 to 75 the tens digit goes from 4 to 7. That is 3 tens, so the jump is +30. Check: 45 + 34 = 79.

items.q: Which number sentence does the number line show?
items.e: It starts at 29 and jumps +50 and +6. 50 + 6 = 56, so it shows 29 + 56 = 85.

items.q: Count on to find the difference. What is 52 − 47?
items.e: The numbers are close, so count on from 47. 47 + 3 = 50. 50 + 2 = 52. The jumps are 3 + 2 = 5. So 52 − 47 = 5.

items.q: Count on to find the difference. What is 83 − 77?
items.e: The numbers are close, so count on from 77. 77 + 3 = 80. 80 + 3 = 83. The jumps are 3 + 3 = 6. So 83 − 77 = 6.

items.q: 19 is 1 less than 20. Add 20, then take away 1. What is 46 + 19?
items.e: Add 20, then take away 1. 46 + 20 = 66. 66 − 1 = 65. (66 forgets to take away 1.)

items.q: 29 is 1 less than 30. Take away 30, then add 1. What is 73 − 29?
items.e: Take away 30, then add 1. 73 − 30 = 43. 43 + 1 = 44. You took away 1 too many, so add 1 back.

items.q: Jump to the next ten. What is 87 + 46?
Start at 64. Jump forward 50, then 6, then 2. Where do you land?

The MAB show 52. You need to take away 17. There are not enough ones. What do you do?
items.e: 52 has only 2 ones, and you need to take away 7. Regroup 1 ten as 10 ones. Then there are 12 ones. Doing 7 − 2 instead is a common mistake.

items.q: You regroup 1 ten in 52. What does 52 look like now?
items.e: Take 1 ten from the 5 tens: 4 tens are left. The 10 ones join the 2 ones: 12 ones. So 52 = 4 tens and 12 ones. Check: 40 + 12 = 52.

items.q: 43 − 18. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones: 3 tens and 13 ones. 18 is crossed out. What is 43 − 18?
items.e: 43 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 3 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 8 = 5. Tens: 3 − 1 = 2. 43 − 18 = 25.

items.q: 61 − 25. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones: 5 tens and 11 ones. 25 is crossed out. What is 61 − 25?
items.e: 61 has only 1 one, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 tens and 11 ones. Ones: 11 − 5 = 6. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. 61 − 25 = 36.

items.q: 74 − 36. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones: 6 tens and 14 ones. 36 is crossed out. What is 74 − 36?
items.e: 74 has only 4 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 6 tens and 14 ones. Ones: 14 − 6 = 8. Tens: 6 − 3 = 3. 74 − 36 = 38.

items.q: 35 − 19. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones: 2 tens and 15 ones. 19 is crossed out. What is 35 − 19?
items.e: 35 has only 5 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 2 tens and 15 ones. Ones: 15 − 9 = 6. Tens: 2 − 1 = 1. 35 − 19 = 16.

items.q: 82 − 46. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones: 7 tens and 12 ones. 46 is crossed out. What is 82 − 46?
items.e: 82 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 7 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 6 = 6. Tens: 7 − 4 = 3. 82 − 46 = 36.

items.q: 53 − 8. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones: 4 tens and 13 ones. 8 is crossed out. What is 53 − 8?
items.e: 53 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 4 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 8 = 5. 4 tens are left. 53 − 8 = 45.

items.q: 90 − 34. 1 ten was regrouped as 10 ones: 8 tens and 10 ones. 34 is crossed out. What is 90 − 34?
items.e: 90 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 8 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 4 = 6. Tens: 8 − 3 = 5. 90 − 34 = 56.

items.q: Mia says 52 − 17 = 45. What mistake did she make?
items.e: In the ones, Mia took 2 from 7. But it must be 2 − 7, and you cannot take 7 from 2. Regroup: 12 − 7 = 5 and 4 − 1 = 3. So 52 − 17 = 35. Her mistake: she did 7 − 2.

items.q: The MAB show 64. What is 64 − 27?
items.e: 64 has only 4 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 tens and 14 ones. Ones: 14 − 7 = 7. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. 64 − 27 = 37.

items.q: What is 91 − 45?
items.e: 91 has only 1 one, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 8 tens and 11 ones. Ones: 11 − 5 = 6. Tens: 8 − 4 = 4. 91 − 45 = 46.
70 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 6 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 4 = 6. Tens: 6 − 3 = 3. 70 − 34 = 36.

items.q: What is 56 − 29?
items.e: 56 has only 6 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 4 tens and 16 ones. Ones: 16 − 9 = 7. Tens: 4 − 2 = 2. 56 − 29 = 27.
83 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 7 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 7 = 6. Tens: 7 − 5 = 2. 83 − 57 = 26.

items.q: What is 45 − 26?
items.e: 45 has only 5 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 3 tens and 15 ones. Ones: 15 − 6 = 9. Tens: 3 − 2 = 1. 45 − 26 = 19.

items.q: What is 92 − 68?
items.e: 92 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 8 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 8 = 4. Tens: 8 − 6 = 2. 92 − 68 = 24.

items.q: 64 − 27 = 37. Which addition checks the answer?
items.e: Add the answer and the number you took away. You should get back to the start: 37 + 27 = 64.

items.q: Find the missing number: 52 − ? = 35
Which subtraction needs regrouping?
items.e: In 63 − 28, there are only 3 ones and you need to take away 8. So regroup 1 ten. In the others, the top ones digit is big enough.

items.q: A bucket has 34 shells. Ruby finds 25 more shells. How many shells are in the bucket now?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 30 + 20 = 50. Ones: 4 + 5 = 9. 50 + 9 = 59.

items.q: The canteen sold 46 icy poles at recess and 38 at lunch. How many icy poles did it sell altogether?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 40 + 30 = 70. Ones: 6 + 8 = 14. 14 ones is 1 ten and 4 ones. 70 + 14 = 84.

items.q: There are 57 students on the bus. 23 students get off at the pool. How many students are still on the bus?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. Tens: 50 − 20 = 30. Ones: 7 − 3 = 4. 30 + 4 = 34.

items.q: Isla has 62 footy cards. She gives 27 cards to her brother. How many cards does she have left?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 62 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 7 = 5. Tens: 5 − 2 = 3. 62 − 27 = 35.

items.q: Which number sentence finds the missing part?
items.e: The whole is 63. One part is 28. Take the part away from the whole: 63 − 28 = ?. The missing part is 35.

items.q: Which number sentence finds the whole?
items.e: The parts are 45 and 36. Put the parts together to find the whole: 45 + 36 = ?. The whole is 81.

items.q: The sausage sizzle cooked 75 sausages. 48 sausages were sold. How many sausages are left?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 75 has only 5 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 6 tens and 15 ones. Ones: 15 − 8 = 7. Tens: 6 − 4 = 2. 75 − 48 = 27.

items.q: Our cricket team scored 68 runs before lunch and 57 runs after lunch. How many runs did we score?
items.e: The bar model shows two parts. Find the whole, so add. Tens: 60 + 50 = 110. Ones: 8 + 7 = 15. 15 ones is 1 ten and 5 ones. 110 + 15 = 125.

items.q: Year 2 needs 90 cans for a recycling project. They have 54 cans. How many more cans do they need?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 90 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 8 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 4 = 6. Tens: 8 − 5 = 3. 90 − 54 = 36.

items.q: Leo has $45. He buys a book for $28. How much money does he have left?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 45 has only 5 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 3 tens and 15 ones. Ones: 15 − 8 = 7. Tens: 3 − 2 = 1. 45 − 28 = 17.

items.q: 83 people watch a race at the swimming carnival. 47 of them are students. The rest are parents. How many parents are there?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 83 has only 3 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 7 tens and 13 ones. Ones: 13 − 7 = 6. Tens: 7 − 4 = 3. 83 − 47 = 36.

items.q: Mia scored 52 points in a game. Jack scored 37 points. How many more points did Mia score?
items.e: How many more means find the difference, so subtract. 52 has only 2 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 4 tens and 12 ones. Ones: 12 − 7 = 5. Tens: 4 − 3 = 1. 52 − 37 = 15.

items.q: Some students were in the library. 14 more students came in. Now there are 31. How many students were there at first?
items.e: The whole is 31. One part is 14. Subtract: 31 has only 1 one, so regroup 1 ten: 2 tens and 11 ones. 11 − 4 = 7. 2 − 1 = 1. 31 − 14 = 17. Check: 17 + 14 = 31.

items.q: The class garden has 26 carrot plants and 39 lettuce plants. How many plants are there altogether?
items.e: Altogether means add. Tens: 20 + 30 = 50. Ones: 6 + 9 = 15. 15 ones is 1 ten and 5 ones. 50 + 15 = 65.

items.q: A netball team scored 18 goals in the first half and 23 goals in the second half. How many goals did it score?
items.e: Put the two halves together, so add. Tens: 10 + 20 = 30. Ones: 8 + 3 = 11. 11 ones is 1 ten and 1 one. 30 + 11 = 41.

items.q: Grace had some stickers. She gave away 25 stickers. Now she has 38. How many stickers did she have at the start?
items.e: The stickers she gave away and the stickers she has now make the whole. Add: 25 + 38. Tens: 20 + 30 = 50. Ones: 5 + 8 = 13. 50 + 13 = 63. Check: 63 − 25 = 38.

items.q: There are 45 children at the beach. 18 children go home. Then 26 more children come. How many children are at the beach now?
Aarav has 72 marbles. He loses 35 marbles. Which number sentence finds how many are left?
items.e: He loses some, so take away. Start with 72 and take away 35: 72 − 35 = ?. The answer is 37.

items.q: A bus has 60 seats. 43 students are sitting down. How many seats are empty?
items.e: You know the whole and one part. Find the other part, so subtract. 60 has 0 ones, so regroup 1 ten as 10 ones: 5 tens and 10 ones. Ones: 10 − 3 = 7. Tens: 5 − 4 = 1. 60 − 43 = 17.

items.q: Charlotte read 34 pages on Saturday and 47 pages on Sunday. How many pages did she read?
items.e: Put the two days together, so add. Tens: 30 + 40 = 70. Ones: 4 + 7 = 11. 11 ones is 1 ten and 1 one. 70 + 11 = 81.
